description:
FILED s540b (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-13), docs/speed-low-hanging-review-s540.md THE LIST.  Code sha 05806e16.

WHERE: lib/POSIX.pm `strftime` (line 304): `my $t = mktime(@f[0..5]); my @l = CORE::localtime($t); return _format_time($fmt, \@l, $t)` -- a round trip through epoch seconds to normalise the fields, each half calling libc's tzset (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp %p-libc-localtime calls tzset on every call, as it must for $ENV{TZ}); then _format_time walks the format one character at a time with substr and a %STRF_SIMPLE lookup, _strf_one per conversion.  perl's POSIX::strftime normalises with mini_mktime (no time zone) and calls libc strftime once.

MEASUREMENT (scratch/s540b/shim/m-strftime.pl, 30,000 calls of strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S', gmtime(1700000000)); sb-sprof: foreign function fstatat 24 %, %make-p-box 10.5 %, p-sprintf 12.6 % total; shimbench quiet numbers legs/leg4.log): PCL 18 us a call, perl 2.2 us.
Prevalence: 80 strftime sites in 21 files (logging, HTTP::Date-like code, Time::Piece users).

THE FIX (two halves, either alone pays): (a) normalise the fields WITHOUT a time zone (mini_mktime's arithmetic: days-from-civil + the yday/wday of the result) so only ONE tzset happens, and only when the format names a zone-dependent conversion (%Z %z %s %c %x %X ...); (b) a `builtin::` over libc strftime through sb-alien (the struct %pcl-c-tm the runtime already declares), the shim keeping the argument checks.  (b) also gives the locale's %c / %x for free -- check perl's output under LC_TIME=C first.

BAR: POSIX strftime rows in Pl/t and the companion's ext/POSIX/t/time.t one-file run, guard rows for every conversion against perl, out-of-range fields (mday 0, mon 12 -> normalised), negative / pre-1970 times, TZ set at run time; the measurement reproduced.

=== QUIET NUMBERS (s540b legs/leg4.log, load 1.1-1.4) === strftime: PCL 15,543 ns a call, perl XS 1,948.

=== s540 (2026-11-13) === scheduled: s540/s540e-prompt.md (the USER: the speed fixing is a normal task).
subject: PERF (s540b, measured): POSIX::strftime's shim calls mktime AND localtime (two tzset, each an fstatat of /etc/localtime -- 24 % of a strftime loop) and then formats in Perl -- 18 us a call under PCL, perl 2.2 us
